verdict: Lilly's revenue jumped 39% to $24.4B on Mounjaro and Zepbound — and the profit line still absorbed a $4.2B charge for buying early-stage research.

segments.name: Mounjaro
segments.note: The diabetes shot (tirzepatide) — Lilly's biggest product, up 65% on volume growth around the world.

segments.name: Zepbound
segments.note: The weight-loss version of tirzepatide — up 49% in the U.S., held back slightly by lower realized prices.

segments.name: All other medicines
segments.note: Everything else — Jardiance, Verzenio, Taltz and the rest — including $410M of Jardiance milestone payments this quarter.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Lilly's own drug research — 17% of revenue, up 23% as the pipeline grows.

opex.name: Marketing, selling & administrative
opex.note: Selling and promoting the medicines — up 14% behind ongoing and planned launches.

opex.name: Acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research bought through acquisitions (mainly AtaiBeckley and Curevo) and expensed immediately — $4.57 of the quarter's EPS.

opex.name: Asset impairment & restructuring
opex.note: A partial impairment of an intangible asset for a molecule in development, plus related charges.

takeaways.title: Two drugs are the company
takeaways.text: Mounjaro ($10.7B, +65%) and Zepbound ($5.4B, +49%) brought in $16.1B — two-thirds of all revenue. Lilly also raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $91–92B.

takeaways.title: The IPR&D charge
takeaways.text: Buying AtaiBeckley and Curevo cost a $4.2B immediate research charge — $4.57 per share, roughly the size of the entire quarterly R&D budget. Reported EPS of $7.22 already includes it.

takeaways.title: Medicines are cheap to make
takeaways.text: Gross margin hit 83.9% — it costs Lilly about 16 cents to manufacture each $1 of medicine it sells, helped by a favorable product mix.

oneTimers: Acquired IPR&D charges of $4,181M — mostly the AtaiBeckley and Curevo acquisitions — expensed in full this quarter. They account for $4.57 of EPS and, being largely nondeductible, pushed the effective tax rate up to 23.3%.
Revenue included about $900M of one-off benefits: $410M of Jardiance sales milestones (the last of them — no further milestones remain) plus favorable adjustments to rebate and discount estimates.
footerNote: Lilly's non-GAAP EPS was $7.48 (vs $7.22 reported); both figures include the $4.57 of acquired IPR&D charges.
